Qt uses a controller-global ImageRendererCache. Native owns one cache per Main binding incarnation, shared by its real preview, still viewer, archive/delete and duplicate filter; standalone duplicate filters own separate policy-bound caches. Final Bound-clone drop, rebind and accepted close permanently retire admission while retained worker/callback handles cannot revive it.

Full still-image cache bytes are pending metadata RGB estimates and loaded RGB/RGBA raster bytes recounted at access. The cache admits one incoming item above its soft bound until maintenance, matching Qt. Pending decoders, accepted per-page 64MiB preview snapshots, current canvas/source/resize buffers, Slint image copies, playback and total process/GPU memory are separate presentation/resource ownership and are not evicted or counted as cache bytes.

Percentage uses strict estimated-size admission and applies only to future misses; existing admitted renderers remain subject to ordinary byte/idle maintenance. Saved policy and ICC changes refresh without resetting current accepted media, zoom, generation/page identity or viewing intervals. Future duplicate copies can only reuse cache-owned full rasters, while the current presentation remains independently retained.

Failed full-image and non-image thumbnail/poster fallback remain uncached; decoder injection keeps the public preview Decoder contract and bypasses the production cache. Existing worker bounds and late-publication generation guards are retained. Imported partial resolution falls back to100x100 exactly; real media metadata/ICC identity displaces stale cached sources.

Inline native duration fields preserve untouched raw299 seconds and enforce the actual300-second edit minimum; the Qt duration-popup geometry is a separate presentation difference. Monitor screen estimates use the owning physical monitor converted to logical size; headless windows without a monitor omit that caption rather than invent screen dimensions.
Validation is Linux only at this exact source and run; Windows and macOS are explicitly deferred, not passed.

claims.behavior: Actual default25/10..50 spinbox plus reference pixel/resolution caption and over-budget warning stages/saves/imports/reopens; passive raw normalization preserves concurrent explicit values. Real viewer/archive/duplicate ordered passes count current and ready actual RGB/RGBA bytes, abort on pending/unknown/refusal, admit only one miss, and honor exact total budget plus separate single limit. Finished-only cache flush is atomic, equality remains allowed for warm work and strict for cache admission; hidden work/lifetime/current-presentation boundaries match recorded policy.
caveats: Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, prefetch/shared renderer backend families, tile/video/cache-delay and the separate duplicate-pair-count control receive zero credit.

The represented GeneralImage full-resolution raster path admits only the effective supported native static-image display action. Qt global renderer/controller ownership, image-project/unsupported codecs, tile/GPU/video renderer prefetch remain broader Partial boundaries.

One lazily started worker per viewer owner admits at most one real miss per readiness pass and coalesces one latest pending navigation. Saved policy and ICC/candidate-action changes capture a new navigation generation. Cache finished-image notifications resume the same captured generation, including another owner’s completion, without publishing SetMedia or viewing intervals. Idle/pending waits hold no Store; in-flight existing disk IO retains its Store until completion and is never joined on the UI.

Current native rendering reuses ready shared Arc rasters but performs its pre-existing synchronous decode independently while warm work is pending. Duplicate overlap decode remains a broader renderer architecture difference from Qt shared asynchronous current-renderer objects; it does not evade the warm budget or count presentation references as cache bytes.

Current image prefix and circular wrap duplicates count their ready actual bytes exactly as Qt. Unknown-resolution misses abort; refusal blocks later small candidates. Total/single prefetch thresholds allow equality, cache admission remains strict, and an uncached successful equality decode repeats on readiness. Atomic easy-space flushing scans only finished entries and deletes none when strict free-space > incoming estimate cannot be reached.

Hidden viewers may continue admitted warm work, as real Qt Canvas does. Close/replacement/rebind/accepted Main close and final Bound-clone drop retire admission; retained GUI/cache handles cannot revive it. Current pixels/zoom/viewing intervals and accepted preview-page snapshots remain independently owned.

Decode failures retain existing native blank/fallback behavior rather than creating Qt error-placeholder renderers. Public preview Decoder injection, two-worker publication bounds, late page/generation guards and ICC identity remain unchanged. Duplicate count is imported/defaulted for this percentage consumer only; no duplicate-count Options row or leaf credit is added.
